home.title: Got something a bit sus, mate?
home.subtitle: Chuck it in below — links, texts, emails and phone numbers — and we'll give it the once-over. What you paste isn't stored, and we never open its links.
check.ocr.timeout: OCR is taking too long — try again or paste the text in yourself.
check.ocr.failed: Couldn't process that image — try a clearer screenshot or paste the text in yourself.
check.ocr.noText: Couldn't read any text from that image — try a clearer screenshot, mate.
check.shareCopied: Copied — flick it to whoever needs to see it
check.dropHint: On a computer you can also chuck a .eml file or screenshot onto this box.
check.forward.heading: Rather flick it over from your email app?
check.forward.body: We'll email you back a verdict.
check.forward.noopen: **Forward it without opening** — swipe or right-click it in your inbox list. Opening loads its tracking pixel, which tells the sender your address is live. Already opened it? Forward it anyway.
check.forward.note: Forwarding goes via your mail provider's servers; pasting stays on your device. If it's really sensitive, paste it instead.
check.help.photo.body: Point your camera dead-on at the message or QR code in decent light, fill the frame, and keep it steady. We'll decode QR codes and read the text for you.
check.help.image.body: A clear screenshot of the whole message is the go. Any format (PNG, JPG, HEIC) is fine — just make sure the text and any links are readable.
check.placeholder: Paste the sus stuff here — link, number, text message, whatever you've got…
check.serverError: Couldn't run that check just now. Give it another crack.
verdict.safe.label: Looks alright, mate
verdict.safe.sub: She's apples — no red flags. Still keep your wits about ya.
verdict.suspicious.label: Something's a bit off
verdict.suspicious.sub: Bit sus, wouldn't trust it. Don't engage until you've checked it out.
verdict.suspicious.step1: Don't click any links — track down the contact yourself
verdict.suspicious.step2: Don't hand over any personal or financial info
verdict.suspicious.step3: Ring the organisation directly using a number you found yourself
verdict.likely_scam.label: Scam alert — don't touch it
verdict.likely_scam.sub: Bloody scammers. Delete it, block them, report it.
verdict.likely_scam.nextSteps: Here's what to do right now:
verdict.likely_scam.step1: Don't click any links or ring any numbers from this thing
verdict.likely_scam.step2: Block the mongrel and delete the message
verdict.likely_scam.step3: If you gave 'em your bank details, call your bank right now
verdict.likely_scam.step4: Report the scam to Scamwatch — scamwatch.gov.au
verdict.unknown.label: Couldn't work it out
verdict.unknown.sub: Not enough to go on, mate — trust your gut.
tracking.heading: Sneaky tracking in this email
tracking.none: No tracking tricks went off — and since we read the source without rendering it, nothing here ever phoned home.
tracking.safe: Opening this in a preview-happy mail app could've set off the stuff above. We read the source without rendering it, so none of it fired here.

verdict.coverage.title: We're a bit thin on the ground here
verdict.coverage.body: We haven't built out our full scam rules for your part of the world yet. We still ran the universal checks — links, shorteners, trackers, and anyone fishing for your personal details — but we can't be as thorough as we are on home turf.
verdict.coverage.advice: A quiet result here means "not checked", not "all clear".
verdict.coverage.learn: What to keep an eye out for:
verdict.overall.heading: The verdict
verdict.breakdown.heading: What we had a squiz at
email.analysis.heading: Who really sent this
email.analysis.clean: No dodgy sender tricks in the headers, far as we can tell.
phone.wangiri.body: Scammers ring once and hang up. Ring back and you cop international premium rates. **Don't call back, no matter what.**
phone.spoof.body: Yep — scammers can chuck any number they like on your caller ID. Costs them nothing and happens all the time. Only the phone company knows the real source, and only the police can trace it.
report.ids.hint: Grab any contact details so others can spot the same scam a mile off.
report.error: Couldn't lodge that report just now. Give it another crack.
report.success.title: Good on ya — you've helped protect others.
report.success.body: Your report's been logged. Every one helps warn the next person about this scam.
report.success.total: {n} reports lodged by Aussies like you.
subs.empty.title: No reports match these filters, mate
bug.sent.title: Cheers — that helps us improve
bug.sent.body: Your report's been logged. Every one helps us make Just Checking, Mate more reliable.
bug.error: Couldn't send that report just now. Give it another crack.
learn.headline: How the mongrels **operate**
learn.tactics.intro: Nearly every scam runs the same handful of mind games. Spot the trick and the spell breaks.
learn.caught.intro: Don't panic, and don't be embarrassed — this happens to switched-on people too. Move quick, based on what you shared.
learn.handle.1: **Slow down.** No legit mob minds you taking your time to check.
learn.handle.5: **Block & delete** the mongrel once you're sure.
learn.report.body: Reporting helps the authorities warn others and put scammers out of business. This tool gives a best-effort check only — **it can't promise to catch every scam** — so trust your gut too.
learn.calendar.body: Scams follow the calendar — tax time, the big sales, the Christmas parcel rush. Knowing what's about makes the odd one out easier to pick.
calendar.intro: Scammers follow the calendar, because a message only works when it looks fair dinkum. Knowing what's about makes the odd one out easier to pick.
calendar.neutrality: Background knowledge only — we give every message the same once-over, whatever the date.
calendar.outro: Out of season doesn't mean you're right. These run all year — they just work best when you're half expecting them.
calendar.empty.body: We only put up seasonal patterns for places we've actually done the legwork on. Having a guess at another country's tax dates would be worse than saying nothing.
radar.intro: What's actually going round {region} right now, pulled from our weekly look at the scam reporting. Each one tells you straight whether we catch it yet.
radar.neutrality: Background knowledge only — being on this list doesn't change how we score a message.
radar.active.heading: Going round right now
radar.watchlist.heading: Gone quiet, but not gone
radar.coverage.none.body: No rule for this one yet, and we'd rather say so. The advice above is what's protecting you.
radar.coverage.na.body: This one happens on a call or on paper, so there's no message for us to have a squiz at. Knowing the script is the defence.
radar.empty.body: We only put up live campaign data for places we've actually done the legwork on. Showing you another country's scams would be worse than showing you none.
radar.method.body: We go through scam reporting from government bodies, security researchers and local sources every week. What's here gets promoted by hand off the back of that — nothing's pulled in automatically, because the sources worth trusting most don't publish feeds.
home.radar.heading: Going round right now
radar.gaps.heading: Worth knowing we don't catch
footer.scope: Universal checks run worldwide. Full rules where we've done the legwork.
subs.lede: Every report gets scrubbed of personal details before it's stored or shown. Reports help people know what's about — they don't change how we score.
